clue.text: Indignant sons joined forces

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son or sons in family trees
to team up is to join forces with someone

explanation.surface: A parent's sons resentfully gang up together against them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being steamed up is an informal idiom for being angry and worked up, as an indignant person is.

clue.text: One who cries half-heartedly without having a drink

indicators.note: half the heart, one of the two middle letters, is removed from the word

parts.note: a sobber is one who sobs or cries

explanation.surface: A weeper cries without real conviction because there is no drink to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sober means not having drunk any alcohol, so being without a drink fits.

clue.text: Serious musical ability — something birds build up

parts.note: a musical person is said to have an ear for music
birds build up a nest from twigs

explanation.surface: Solemn musical talent is something like a nest that birds construct.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest and serious are synonyms for someone sincere and intense in manner.

clue.text: Crew works to get in position

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
an oeuvre is the body of an artist's works

explanation.surface: A crew labours to move a ship into position.
explanation.definitionFit: To manoeuvre is to move carefully into a required place, so it means get in position.

clue.text: Decline to discourage start of Irish pontificate

parts.note: to deter is to discourage

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of the word Irish

parts.note: to orate is to speak pompously, to pontificate

explanation.surface: A churchman refuses to put off the start of an Irish papacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a verb of refusal and 'pontificate' like a papal reign, but each is a verb: grow worse, and speak pompously.
explanation.definitionFit: To deteriorate is to get worse over time, which is to decline.

clue.text: A lot of fruit and some veg

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, means the fruit word loses its last letter

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Plenty of fruit along with a few vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea is a green vegetable, so it is an example of veg.

clue.text: Current breaking up fish grounds

indicators.note: the current symbol breaks the fish word apart, splitting it to sit in the middle

parts.note: the bass is a common sea and freshwater fish
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: An ocean current breaks up a fishing area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' looks like fishing grounds in the surface, but it is a noun meaning reasons, defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds for a decision are its foundation or underlying reason, a synonym for basis.

clue.text: Able follower once — one generating turnover, perhaps

definitions.meaning: in the old phonetic alphabet Able was followed by ... for the letter B
a pastry cook makes apple turnovers among other bakes

explanation.surface: A capable deputy of former days creates high business turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like business revenue, but it is a fruit pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Baker was the old radio code word for B after Able, and a bread maker turns out pastries such as turnovers.

clue.text: Sales pitch about a new breed of dog

indicators.note: the sales pitch word goes about, surrounding, the other letters

parts.note: a spiel is a glib persuasive sales talk

explanation.surface: A dealer's patter about a new breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The spaniel is a breed of dog with long drooping ears, such as the cocker.

clue.text: Revolutionary is outside fomenting unrest

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning, so the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel is out in the streets stirring up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like the definition, but it is the anagram signal; the definition is 'fomenting unrest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seditious speech or action incites rebellion against authority, which is stirring up unrest.

clue.text: Soul singer needing backing for a title

parts.note: in ancient Egyptian religion the ba is the soul

indicators.note: backing means the singer word is read from right to left

parts.note: a tenor is a high male singer

explanation.surface: A soul music singer needs a backing group before he can get a recording title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soul' and 'backing' sound like music, but soul gives the Egyptian BA and backing turns the singer around.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronetcy is a hereditary British rank, so the word names an honour and its holder: a title.

clue.text: A seven days period of conflict with daughter being difficult

parts.note: WK is the abbreviation for week, a seven-day period
a war is a period of armed conflict
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A week of fighting with one's daughter makes for a tricky time.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward and difficult are synonyms for something hard to handle or a person hard to deal with.

clue.text: Old magistrate always backed imprisoning English

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the English letter captive inside it
backed means the word for always is turned to read backwards

parts.note: ever is an old word for always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A former magistrate who constantly supported jailing the English.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval England a reeve was a local official who kept the peace, a kind of magistrate of old.

clue.text: Control what teacher does in time off work

indicators.note: the teaching word goes in the rest word, splitting it before its final letter

parts.note: a rest is a break or time off from work
a teacher trains pupils

explanation.surface: Discipline is what a teacher shows during the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is self-control or the act of holding something in check, a synonym for control.

clue.text: In the event, photo needs something done on greens

parts.note: a shot is a photograph
putting is the golf stroke played on the green

explanation.surface: At the occasion, a photograph needs some work done on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greens' looks like vegetables or lawns but means golf greens.
explanation.definitionFit: The shot put is a field athletics discipline, so this throwing is an event at a meeting.

clue.text: Flirts regularly — that's socially acceptable

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word flirts, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone who flirts often is told that this behaviour is fine in company.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit can mean suitable or proper by social standards, as in a remark not fit for polite company.

clue.text: A lot of artillery being used to sack country

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
a power is a nation with influence, such as a world power

explanation.surface: Heavy guns are deployed to plunder a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like pillage in the surface but means dismiss from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Firepower is the destructive capacity of guns, so a lot of artillery is a strong fit.

clue.text: Instrument Vince plays with three learners and old, old, Oscar

indicators.note: to play with something is to fiddle about with it, so these letters are toyed with and rearranged

parts.words: three learners and old, old, Oscar
parts.note: L is the learner plate symbol, so three learners give three Ls; O abbreviates old, twice, and Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A musician called Vince plays an instrument alongside three students and some elderly people named Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays with' signals the anagram of VINCE, LLL and OOO together.
explanation.definitionFit: The violoncello is the full formal name of the cello, a stringed instrument.

clue.text: Reminder of reported nickname of Prague piano virtuoso?

indicators.note: reported means the phrase is said aloud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a brilliant pianist from Prague might be dubbed the Czech Liszt, after the Hungarian virtuoso Franz Liszt

explanation.surface: A note recalling a reputed nickname of a great Prague pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: A checklist is a list of items to tick off, serving as a reminder of what to do.

clue.text: Repent a plot involving corrupt team member

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters are spoilt and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A player in a team is accused of corruption and told to repent of his plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' does double duty in sense, but in the parse it is the anagram signal; the definition is the rest of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotten apple is an idiom for one bad member who spoils the rest of a group or team.

clue.text: Old city contains lines with key mode of transport

indicators.note: the old city name contains the other letters within it

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad
L is an abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An ancient city has railway lines and a key means of transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolley, such as a trolleybus or American streetcar, is a means of getting around.

clue.text: Short cut to get fuel

indicators.note: short means the word for a cut loses its final letter

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut

explanation.surface: A brief way to obtain fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is a fuel, both natural gas for heating and, in American usage, petrol.

clue.text: Thickened water ice using egg in a mixture of agar

indicators.note: the egg word goes in the scrambled letters, near the end
a mixture of means the letters of agar are mixed into a new order

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: A recipe for a frozen dessert thickened with egg and agar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' is the louse's egg, not a hen's, which is why it can sit inside the jumbled agar.
explanation.definitionFit: A granita is an Italian dessert of coarse, grainy frozen sweetened water, a type of water ice.

clue.text: Advocate of support unit not being left empty

parts.note: a prop is a support
one is the unit number

indicators.note: the word not is emptied of its middle letter, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A supporter of a backing group refuses to let the place stand empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A proponent is someone who argues in favour of a cause, the same as an advocate.

clue.text: Australia has a certain invigorating air

parts.note: Oz is an informal name for Australia
one can mean a certain, as in one Mr Smith

explanation.surface: Australia has a particular bracing climate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is used informally for fresh, bracing sea air thought to be good for health.

clue.text: Bent half of a German sausage

indicators.note: half of means only the first part of the sausage name is used

parts.note: knackwurst is a short, plump German sausage

explanation.surface: A German sausage curved in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like it describes the sausage, but it is a noun meaning a natural talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural aptitude or talent, which is what a knack is.

clue.text: Cut cabbage the nation over for rich peasant

indicators.note: over means the joined letters are turned over to read backwards
cut means the cabbage word loses its last letter

parts.note: kale is a kind of cabbage
UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A wealthy peasant cuts cabbages all over the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Kulaks were relatively prosperous peasant farmers in Tsarist and early Soviet Russia.

clue.text: Rich not working after Spring?

indicators.note: after places the not-working word after the spring word

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
a machine that is off is not working

explanation.surface: Wealthy people who stop working once spring arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well-off means having plenty of money, a synonym for rich.

clue.text: Reduced cost of travel over large distances

indicators.note: reduced means the travel cost word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a fare is the price paid for a journey

explanation.surface: Cheaper ticket prices for long journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Far as an adverb means to or at a great distance, as in travelled far.

clue.text: First piece of writing, one I found in Latin needing going over

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: going over suggests the letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: An opening passage in which a Latin student finds a first-person pronoun that needs revising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' signals the anagram of I, I and LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial is the first letter of a word or name, the opening piece of anything written.

clue.text: Frost, perhaps, recited poem

indicators.note: recited means the word for frost is said out loud, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: rime is a kind of frost formed from freezing fog

explanation.surface: Robert Frost, perhaps, reads one of his poems out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the poet Robert Frost, but it is a sample of hoar frost, RIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme can be a short poem or verse, as in a nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Most appropriate deposit just south of the Thames in London?

definitions.text: just south of the Thames in London?

parts.note: the right thing is the most fitting or appropriate one
to bank money is to deposit it

explanation.surface: The best place to put money in is just south of the river in London.
explanation.walkthrough: A river's banks are named facing downstream, so in London the Thames's right bank is its southern side.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing downstream, the right bank of the Thames lies on its southern edge through London.
